PullRequest.Title: automations: improve 'running' state and automatic refresh
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #341114, #341025, #341113.

## Motivation

Cloud automation cards give no immediate confirmation when a run starts, and remote edits stay stale until a manual refresh. This change adds pending-run feedback, a refresh progress indicator, and automatic refresh while the Automations view is visible.

## Changes made

- Show the shared loading spinner to the right of the card title and replace the prompt with "Starting run..." until a new run appears or the request fails. Fixes [#341114](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341114).
- Replace the Refresh label with an icon that shows the loading spinner during refresh. Background refresh stays clickable; clicking it waits for the active refresh instead of starting another. Cached cards remain editable. Fixes [#341025](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341025).
- Load the list when Automations opens, then refresh every 60 seconds after the previous refresh finishes while the view remains visible. Window focus changes do not trigger requests; manual Refresh remains available. Preserve the provider's existing 15-second active-history and bounded-discovery checks. Fixes [#341113](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/341113).
- Keep Refresh behind the existing automations flag, expose spinner progress with `aria-busy`, and log automatic refresh failures without repeated error toasts. Preserve pending cloud-run feedback when an unrelated host is disconnected.

Manual checks with GitHub sign-in and `chat.automations.enabled` / `chat.automations.cloud.enabled` on:

1. Run a safe manual automation. The spinner appears right of the stationary title, the prompt changes to "Starting run...", and another click cannot dispatch a duplicate. New queued history restores the prompt; a failed request reports an error and clears feedback.
2. Click Refresh from idle, then during a background refresh. The spinner animates; only the click disables the button, and it re-enables when refresh settles. A click during refresh starts no extra request. Open a card while the catalogue is refreshing.
3. Leave Automations visible for 60 seconds after refresh finishes: another refresh starts. Switch away from and back to the window before the next interval: no extra refresh should start. Hide Automations for more than 60 seconds: its list timer stops. Reopening reloads the list.
4. Disable the automations setting: Refresh is hidden. Re-enable it: Refresh returns. Existing active-history polling is unchanged and remains provider-owned.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed timer and call are explicit and tested at a one-minute cadence; the complete transitive call path and every network boundary are visible in repository code. ETag revalidation may reduce response bytes on warm requests, but it does not remove the per-resource network-call fan-out, so only exact latency and prevalence remain uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub network requests, response bytes, JSON parsing/allocation, and credential/transport work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each poll costs O(R + A + H), where R is all remembered/recent repositories, A is all automation definitions fetched in detail, and H is one history-list request per automation plus active-run detail requests. The cost repeats for the entire time the view is visible; the remembered repository set has no storage bound.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive network I/O and background CPU/energy use, with growing refresh duration and rate-limit pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Opening the view performed one explicit full refresh; the same expensive reconciliation was not automatically repeated every minute while the view remained visible. Independent history polling was limited to active/discovery cases.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The visible view now invokes the aggregate full refresh immediately and again 60 seconds after every completion. That refresh traverses every provider and, for the cloud provider, refreshes both the complete catalogue and complete history.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 283 adds a background aggregate refresh inside the newly scheduled one-minute loop; before the diff, the constructor issued only the one entry refresh and had no recurring scheduler.
Findings.Title: Avoid replaying the full per-automation fan-out every minute
Findings.Impact: Leaving the Automations view open continuously generates repeated GitHub traffic and credential/serialization work, can consume rate-limit/network/battery budget, and makes each poll increasingly long for accounts that have accumulated repositories and automations. For example, 10 repositories with 5 automations each cause at least 120 remote calls per tick before active-run detail requests (10 visibility + 10 list + 50 detail + 50 history), repeated roughly every minute.
Findings.Evidence: The added call reaches ProviderAutomationService.refresh -> CloudAutomationStore.refreshCatalogueAndHistory -> GitHubCloudAutomationStore.refreshRepositories and then refreshHistory. For every remembered repository (the storage map is not bounded, plus up to 10 recent workspaces), refreshRepositories performs getRepository, paginated list calls, and api.get for every automation detail in batches of five. refreshHistory then performs listRuns for every cached automation and tasks.get for each active run, with concurrency limited to four. AutomationSummary already exposes updated_at, but the current path refetches every detail even when summaries are unchanged.
Findings.Recommendation: Make the periodic background path incremental rather than calling the full manual-refresh path: use the existing list summaries and their id/updated_at values to reuse cached details and fetch only new or changed definitions, and schedule history refresh independently so an unchanged catalogue tick does not automatically replay both fan-outs. Preserve the existing full reconciliation for entry/manual recovery and uncertain mutations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Leave the Automations custom view visible with cloud automations enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The initial refresh runs on view construction; each subsequent refresh starts 60 seconds after the prior one settles. Cached cards remain usable, so the requests are off the immediate UI critical path, but the scheduler continuously drives remote and filesystem work for the view lifetime.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each non-cloud recent workspace to a GitHub repository by reading git configuration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 10 recent Agents workspaces on every tick, deduplicated later by repository key
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This resolution occurred for entry/manual refreshes, but the diff newly repeats it every minute while the view is visible.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before repository network reconciliation for the tick can finish; repositories are processed serially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Verify repository visibility, list automation summaries/pages, and fetch each automation's full detail
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per tick: one visibility request per effective repository, one list request per page, and one detail request per automation; summaries are grouped in batches of five only for concurrency, not call reduction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The full fan-out ran on entry/manual refresh, not periodically for the whole visible-view lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the card-interaction critical path but all calls must settle before the next history phase and next 60-second delay begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List up to 50 runs for every cached automation and hydrate every active run detail
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One listRuns request per automation plus one tasks.get request per queued/running/waiting run, at aggregate concurrency four.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Full history ran on entry/manual refresh; independent 15-second history polling was limited to active runs or bounded discovery, rather than unconditional minute polling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after catalogue reconciliation and must finish before the timer's next 60-second delay is scheduled.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All persisted cloud-automation repositories (unbounded over account lifetime) plus up to 10 Agents recent workspaces; all automations in those repositories (up to 10 pages of 100 per repository); and up to 50 unarchived runs per automation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only one timer refresh is intended at a time. The cloud definition refresh coalesces concurrent calls with refreshPromise and serializes repository processing; detail GETs run five at a time within each page. History is sequenced after definitions and limits per-automation work to four concurrent queues. Concurrency is bounded, but total call cardinality is not reduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Definitions/history are held in memory and GET transport enables ETag revalidation, so warm responses may be smaller. Nevertheless every tick revalidates every repository, definition, and automation history. Summary id/updated_at values are available but are not used to avoid detail GETs. Failed ticks are retried after 60 seconds; persisted repository references are not bounded or negatively cached away.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the timer cadence, aggregate refresh call, full transitive filesystem/network path, limits, caches, and concurrency are explicit in code and covered by timer tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact repository/automation counts, ETag hit rates, and request latency vary by account. Even modest counts create dozens to hundreds of calls per minute; uncertainty affects severity, not the fan-out mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable high-severity network boundary fan-out: the diff converts a full O(repositories + automations + histories) reconciliation into continuous minute polling without incremental invalidation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click Refresh while an automatic or manual refresh is already running
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The user waits for the active refresh rather than dispatching another; an idle click runs the existing full refresh and remains on that action's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Full provider catalogue and history refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective refresh per provider after UI and store coalescing
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual Refresh already invoked the same provider refresh; this diff changes UI progress/coalescing presentation but does not increase effective concurrent boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Manual action completion waits for the refresh; clicking during an active background refresh starts no additional boundary call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Same repository, automation, and history cardinality as a full refresh, but one effective in-flight refresh per cloud store.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The header suppresses a command if isRefreshing is already true. GitHubCloudAutomationStore.refreshPromise coalesces catalogue calls and historyRefresh coalesces history reads; provider stores run in parallel via Promise.all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm transport ETags apply. Manual refresh intentionally invalidates workspace eligibility; background refresh preserves it. No extra manual request is introduced when the user clicks during a background refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: UI guards and store promises are directly traced and tested.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific refresh costs vary, but effective duplicate-call suppression is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the changed manual-refresh behavior coalesces rather than amplifies concurrent work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click Run now and wait for a newly discovered run
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing provider dispatch remains on the run action's critical path. Added pending feedback snapshots current run IDs and updates card DOM locally while the existing history mechanisms discover the run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for the clicked automation; duplicate card clicks are suppressed while pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Run now already dispatched through the same provider path; the diff changes local feedback lifetime only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must acknowledge dispatch before accepted/started feedback settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Poll run history after dispatch/while active
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing bounded discovery/active polling, with one listRuns per cached automation per history refresh and concurrency four downstream.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The 15-second history scheduler and boundary calls predate the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required for dispatch acknowledgement, but determines when pending visual feedback clears after an accepted cloud request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Snapshot cost grows with the current run list once per click; observable card updates grow with visible automation-card count on run/history state changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The per-card starting state disables duplicate clicks. Provider dispatch concurrency is unchanged; existing history refresh uses its limiter/sequencer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The starting snapshot is retained only until a new matching run or error state and then released. Existing history data remains provider-cached; no new persistent cache or negative-cache behavior is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: run call flow, pending-state cleanup, and existing history ownership are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Visible card/run counts vary; added local Set allocation and DOM writes are bounded by view contents and are small relative to the existing network work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding: duplicate dispatch is suppressed, retained state is cleaned up, and the added local work does not establish a realistic independent regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and traced visible-view refresh, manual coalescing, cloud catalogue/history fan-out, cache behavior, concurrency, filesystem resolution, and run feedback. Submitted one finding for the newly recurring full remote reconciliation; no regression-fix learning signal applies.
